title: The BI blueprint: sources, definitions, tiers and trust
course_title: Business Intelligence Basics: Designing Systems that Drive Decisions

say: The BI blueprint: sources, definitions, tiers and trust.
This is the video for Module 2 of Business Intelligence Basics: designing the BI system.
BI design depends more on a few well-kept documents than on any single software product. Together they make a blueprint that any tool, from Google Sheets to Power BI, can build.
A data source map shows where the data lives.
A metric dictionary says what each number means.
A reporting structure gets the right view to the right person.
And quality checks keep people trusting the numbers.
For every source system, rate three things from 1, poor, to 3, good.

say: A metric dictionary is the single written definition of every key number. Each entry has a meaning, a formula, a source, one owner, and a refresh time.
Here, the owner is the bursar, and it refreshes every Monday by 10 am.
The school billed 48,600,000 naira this term.
It received 39,852,000 naira. Received divided by billed, times 100, is 82%.
Notice the exclusions. If scholarship students stay in the billed figure, the rate looks worse, and the proprietor may chase the wrong families.
You cannot serve every decision at once. Score each one for value from 1 to 5: how much money, time or risk depends on it.

Feasibility 1 to 5: data ready, easy to build
Fourth depot: 5 x 1 = 5, data work first

say: Then score feasibility from 1 to 5: how ready the data is. Multiply the two for a score out of 25.

say: Different people need different views. The strategic tier serves the owner or board, monthly or quarterly, with 5 to 8 headline numbers against targets.

panel.heading: Three tiers, not one crowded page

cards.d: Owner or board, monthly or quarterly. 5 to 8 headline metrics against targets, on one page.
Branch and department managers, weekly. Breakdowns by branch, product or rep: what changed and why.
Supervisors, daily. Lists to act on: low stock, overdue payers, today's deliveries.

say: The tactical tier serves managers weekly, with breakdowns that show what changed and why.

panel.heading: Three tiers, not one crowded page

say: The operational tier serves supervisors daily, with lists, not charts. These 7 retailers are more than 30 days overdue, call them today.
And tie every report to a fixed meeting. If nobody can name the meeting, question whether the report should exist.

say: The first wrong number sends managers back to their private spreadsheets. So check six things every time data refreshes: completeness, uniqueness, consistency, timeliness, validity and accuracy.
For example, Hauwa finds 30 duplicate member IDs in her register of 1,250 records. She fixes problems at the source, not in the report, so they do not come back next month.

panel.heading: Six checks on every refresh
items: Timeliness: refresh date on every report

say: BI brings personal data into one place, which raises the risk. In Nigeria, the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 set up the NDPC to enforce data protection rules. Load only the personal fields a decision really needs.

panel.heading: Data protection habits
items: Load only the personal fields a decision needs
Show totals; names only in action lists
No raw exports in WhatsApp groups

say: Show totals in reports, and keep names and phone numbers only in lists for staff who must act on them.

say: Use strong passwords and two-step verification, and remove access the day someone leaves. Customer lists are valuable to fraudsters, so confirm anyone claiming to be a bank or IT support through a known official contact first.

say: To remember. Rate your sources. Write every metric with its exclusions and one owner. Build the highest scores first.
Use three tiers tied to meetings, fix quality at the source, and protect personal data.
